title: Computing points in connected components defined by a real inequation: algorithms, complexity and implementations, Part I
summary: We consider the problem of computing sample points in each connected component of a semi-algebraic set defined by the non-vanishing or the positivity of an n-variate polynomial of degree d, with rational coefficients of bit size bounded by $τ$. Such a problem is a basic routine in effective real algebraic geometry, used in higher-level algorithms for solving polynomial systems over the reals and finds many applications in sciences. We design a probabilistic algorithm for solving this problem, which is based on reductions to different routines for solving zero-dimensional polynomial systems.…
